goals.title: Wind a motor strong enough to lift a friend
goals.critique: This is round 16's motor again, and the rework answers its main fault: each friend's weight asks for its own coil, so there is a reason to wind a second, different motor, and a friend spinning the wrong way under its own blade is a real physics joke that teaches. The pig drifting over the pond and splashing is a clip people would send. But a hand-wound battery motor lifting a pig is the one thing in it that cannot work by what it is, so either the numbers are quietly cheated, which breaks the human's rule, or nothing heavier than Pinchy ever flies. The cast of friends is short, so the loop ends when the last one is airborne. The road now stacks an unbuilt electromagnetic solver, rotor thrust and friend flight before the first lift-off.

goals.title: Cut sticks into legs and let the sea wind walk them
goals.critique: This is new and the strongest in the human's direction: rigid sticks and pins whose lengths alone decide the gait, a foot path drawn live in the sand while you cut so every millimetre is read and not guessed, and footprints that record how it walked. Daily wind, wet and dry sand and the fixed road of rigid bodies and pin joints are a well-priced, buildable physics bet. But the whole image is Theo Jansen's Strandbeest, so the clip people send is one they have seen before, and once a known good set of lengths is found the six-leg copy step collapses the search. Pins that wear and pop risk feeling like a hidden durability counter unless their looseness is visible.
